rubrics.evidence: The patch removes key_down/key_up/pointer_down/pointer_up/move_to/scroll/tap/type_key from the InputSource trait and deletes all discard-and-return-self implementations from NullActions, KeyActions, MouseActions, PenActions, TouchActions, and WheelActions. InputSource now exposes only pause() and then(). Device-level members are moved to inherent impls only on capable sources: KeyActions::key_down/key_up/type_key, MouseActions/PenActions/TouchActions::pointer_down/pointer_up/move_to/tap, and WheelActions::scroll. No shared trait default for device-level members remains, and no source retains a do-nothing device member.
rubrics.criterion: Every device-level member of the input-sequence builder abstractions (typing key press/release, pointer button press/release, pointer movement, wheel scrolling, and the press-release shorthands) is declared on an abstraction implemented only by the input sources that genuinely queue that kind of event; no input source retains such a member that it satisfies by discarding its arguments and returning the builder unchanged, and no source inherits that kind of member as a shared trait default.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch modifies only src/actions.rs and does not touch src/wd.rs or src/session.rs at all. The smell.diff injected: (1) WebDriverCompatibleCommand declared as `pub trait WebDriverCompatibleCommand: VendorRequestCommand` in src/wd.rs, forcing every implementor to provide vendor_url/vendor_headers; (2) Wcmd in src/session.rs implementing VendorRequestCommand with empty answers (vendor_url returns None, vendor_headers returns Vec::new()); (3) the request path unconditionally consulting cmd.vendor_url() and cmd.vendor_headers() for every command. Since the agent's patch contains no changes to these files, all three vendor-routing smells remain: the general command contract still requires vendor-routing members from every implementor, the internal wrapper still provides them as empty answers, and the request path still consults them for all commands.
rubrics.criterion: Vendor-routing members (per-command URL override, per-command transport headers) are carried only by commands that genuinely participate in vendor routing: the crate's general command contract no longer requires them from every implementor, and the internal wrapper for standard WebDriver commands no longer provides them as empty answers. The repair is acceptable whether the vendor surface is removed together with its integration or kept as an opt-in capability attached only to genuinely vendor-routed commands.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch keeps the universal members on the shared trait: `pub trait InputSource` still declares `fn pause` and `fn then`, and each impl—including `impl InputSource for NullActions`—retains those methods. rubrics.criterion: The members that genuinely apply to every input source type (contributing a pause tick, chaining one raw action payload into the sequence) remain declared on the shared abstraction and stay available on every source, including the null source that contributes only pauses.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only modifies src/actions.rs and never touches src/session.rs or src/wd.rs. The request-issuing path in session.rs therefore still contains the smell's blanket consult: `cmd.vendor_url().map(Ok).unwrap_or_else(|| cmd.endpoint(&self.wdb, self.session.as_deref()))` and `for (name, value) in cmd.vendor_headers() { req = req.header(name, value); }`, which call vendor-routing members on every command regardless of whether it carries vendor routing. The task explicitly requires 'The request path must not consult vendor-routing members of commands that do not carry them,' but no guard, downcast, or restriction was added, so the coupled consumer was not brought in step with the command-surface change.
rubrics.criterion: The session's request-issuing path was brought in step with the command-surface change: it no longer consults vendor-routing members on commands that do not carry them (no dangling call sites or unreachable branches for the removed consult), and request URL derivation goes through the endpoint path for every command that reaches it.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch removes all placeholder-describing text from src/actions.rs. The trait-level doc paragraph stating 'Input sources that do not produce a given kind of device event accept the arguments of the corresponding members without queueing an action for them' is replaced with text describing the new design ('A source does not expose builders for event kinds it cannot generate...instead of silently dropping the unsupported steps'). Obsolete fragments of the removed grouping were left behind: empty or vestigial impl blocks, member groups that remain defined on a type that no longer has any purpose for them, blanket forwarding implementations left in place for an abstraction that no longer exists, or use-declarations that still name abstractions absent from the post-change structure.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state added forwarding conveniences, per-surface declarations, and import entries; a complete repair removes the ones the new design no longer needs instead of abandoning them. Vestigial structure is compile-clean clutter that this item targets.

MouseActions, PenActions, and TouchActions retain `pointer_down`, `pointer_up`, `move_to`, and `tap` (e.g., `MouseActions::new(...).move_to(...).tap(MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT)`). rubrics.evidence: The patch only relocates device builders from the InputSource trait to inherent methods on concrete source types without changing their bodies: KeyActions::key_down still calls self.then(KeyAction::Down { value: key }), MouseActions::tap still chains pointer_down then pointer_up, and WheelActions::scroll still calls self.then(WheelAction::Scroll { duration: None, x: 0, y: 0, delta_x, delta_y }). The trait pause/then members and each impl's then body (self.actions.push(action); self) are unchanged, and no Into<ActionSequence> conversion or perform_actions payload logic is modified, so valid builder chains produce the same tick sequence as before.
